families.title: Probabilistic programs: Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and further systems
families.intro: The programs of the Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and Geni papers, against Dice, Alea.jl and Roulette, and on the programs they take Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, Storm and PRISM. tddlog runs its own encoding of a program's integers (binary, never one-hot) and is asked what the baseline answers: single marginals where the baseline gives single marginals, a distribution's values only where it computes them. Alea.jl's times leave out Julia's start-up and compilation, as its papers time it; the dashed lines add them, and Racket's start-up to Roulette's.

cards.title: The Dice paper's programs
paras: **Against Alea.jl (without Julia's start-up and compilation):** Of the 46 instances both are given, tddlog answers 46 and Alea.jl 40. Over the 46 that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 13.8 s in all and Alea.jl 3 642 s; over the 40 both answer, 4.39 s against 42.2. tddlog alone answers bn_andes, bn_link, bn_munin, dice_diamond_k6400, dice_ladder_k6400 and 1 more.

**Against Dice:** Of the 46 instances both are given, tddlog answers 46 and Dice 29. Over the 46 that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 13.8 s in all and Dice 10 701 s; over the 29 both answer, 2.92 s against 501.2. tddlog is slower on dice_ladder_k6400 (1.24 s against Dice's 0.41), dice_diamond_k6400 (0.51 s against Dice's 0.19), dice_ladder_k1600 (0.41 s against Dice's 0.10) and dice_diamond_k1600 (0.20 s against Dice's 0.07). tddlog alone answers bn_insurance, bn_link, bn_munin, bn_pathfinder, dice_digitRecognition and 12 more.

**Against Roulette:** Of the 46 instances both are given, tddlog answers 46 and Roulette 37. Over the 46 that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 13.8 s in all and Roulette 5 526 s; over the 37 both answer, 3.34 s against 126.0. tddlog alone answers bn_alarm, bn_andes, bn_hailfinder, bn_munin, dice_caesar-iter_k3000 and 4 more.

**Against noDice:** Of the 25 instances both are given, tddlog answers 25 and noDice 19. **Against Genfer:** Both are given 7 instances and answer all of them. Over the 7 both answer, tddlog takes 0.02 s in all and Genfer 0.04 s.

findings.title: Bit-blasted programs
paras: tddlog alone answers genes up to 100 genes in 12 s, where Alea.jl times out at the paper's 5; fair_dt14 up to 32 bits in 71 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 20 (16 s) and times out at 24; fair_dt4 up to 32 bits in 72 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 20 (13 s) and times out at 24; addFun_max up to 29 bits in 51 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 21 (152 s) and runs out of memory at the paper's 23; clickGraph up to 16 bits in under a second, where Alea.jl answers up to 8 and runs out of memory at the paper's 10; tug_of_war up to 28 bits in under a second, where Alea.jl answers up to 20 (159 s) and times out at the paper's 22; addFun_sum up to 29 bits in 1.0 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 23 (432 s) and times out at 25; clinicalTrial2 up to 18 bits in under a second, where Alea.jl answers up to 12 (308 s) and runs out of memory at 14; conjugate_gaussians up to 29 bits in 1.5 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 23 (169 s) and times out at 25; pi up to 20 bits in 185 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 16 (334 s) and times out at 18; clinicalTrial1 up to 10 bits in 52 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 8 (263 s) and runs out of memory at 10; genes5 up to 27 bits in 10 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 25 (81 s) and runs out of memory at 27; normal_mixture_mu1 at the paper's precision (9 bits, 139 s), where Alea.jl answers up to 7 and runs out of memory at the paper's 9; normal_mixture_mu2 at the paper's precision (9 bits, 173 s), where Alea.jl answers up to 7 and runs out of memory at the paper's 9; zeroone_w2 up to 25 bits in 6.8 s, where Alea.jl answers up to 23 (326 s) and runs out of memory at 25; and normal_mixture_theta at the paper's precision (9 bits, 32 s), where Alea.jl runs out of memory at the paper's 9. Against Alea.jl's time without compilation, over the 162 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 5 550 s in all and Alea.jl 18 143 s; over the 135 both answer, 1 743 s against 4 369 s, and tddlog is faster on 64 of the 135 both answer; against Alea.jl's process, over the 162 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 5 550 s in all and Alea.jl 33 300 s; over the 135 both answer, 1 743 s against 18 755 s, and tddlog is faster on 134 of 135.

findings.title: Where Alea.jl leads
paras: On multimodal, a circuit of 4 617 random flips at its smallest size, tddlog runs out of memory at that size with each of its three vtrees and Alea.jl answers, in 31 s there. On conjugate_ex3 and laplace Alea.jl reaches 2 to 4 bits further than tddlog's best vtree. Of the 223 bit-blasted instances that some system ran, tddlog answers 199 (201 with one of its three vtrees), Alea.jl 141 and Dice 17.

findings.title: The paper's samplers
paras: At the paper's precision the exact answer is closer to the model's than any sampler comes in its runs on GPA (2e-16, which tddlog computes in 20 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁴ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 208 s); tug_of_war (5e-7, which tddlog computes in 0.6 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-5 in 52 s); conjugate_gaussians (5e-6, which tddlog computes in 0.9 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-4 in 71 s); zeroone_w1 (9e-5, which tddlog computes in 0.3 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 2e-1 in 102 s); zeroone_w2 (5e-4, which tddlog computes in 1.3 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 1e-1 in 102 s); addFun_sum (4e-6, which tddlog computes in 0.7 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 7e-4 in 7.3 s); clinicalTrial1 (5e-16, which tddlog computes in 1.7 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 311 s); clinicalTrial2 (7e-7, which tddlog computes in 0.02 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 1e-4 in 87 s); and addFun_max (3e-7, which tddlog computes in 37 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-4 in 68 s). On normal_mixture_mu1, normal_mixture_mu2, trueskill and conjugate_ex3 a sampler comes as close to the model as the exact answer at the paper's precision, sooner than the exact systems answer. Stan's HMC does not converge on altermu2, multimodal, zeroone_w1 and zeroone_w2: its error at its largest sample count stays above 1% of the answer.

findings.title: Roulette's programs
paras: tddlog reaches the largest size on caesar, diamond, the hmm's filtering joint, the hmm's filtering marginal, the hmm's marginal likelihood, the hmm's smoothing joint, the hmm's smoothing marginal, ladder, motivating and network, or ties and is fastest there. Dice reaches the largest size on hardware, or ties and is fastest there. On the nine networks tddlog answers 9, Roulette 9, Dice 8 and Alea.jl 9. In total time: against Roulette, over the 65 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 89 s in all and Roulette 15 118 s; over the 40 both answer, 3.8 s against 118 s; against Dice, over the 75 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 224 s in all and Dice 22 431 s; over the 40 both answer, 44 s against 1 431 s; and against Alea.jl, over the 71 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 112 s in all and Alea.jl 6 560 s; over the 61 both answer, 36 s against 560 s. Of the 88 instances that some system ran, tddlog answers 88, Roulette 40, Dice 40 and Alea.jl 61.

findings.title: Geni's programs
paras: tddlog leads on the grid, router failures: it answers up to 20×20 (4.5 s) and runs out of memory at 24×24, where Dice answers up to 16×16 (78 s) and times out at 18×18, Alea.jl answers up to 14×14 (101 s) and runs out of memory at 16×16 and ProbLog answers up to 6×6 (12 s) and times out at 8×8. Dice leads on the grid, link failures: it answers up to 16×16 (331 s) and times out at 18×18, where tddlog answers up to 14×14 (22 s) and runs out of memory at 16×16, Alea.jl answers up to 14×14 (132 s) and times out at 16×16 and ProbLog answers up to 6×6 (5.6 s) and times out at 8×8. tddlog leads on the weather factory, by factories: it answers up to 16 factories (18 s) and runs out of memory at 17 factories, where Dice answers up to 16 factories (385 s) and times out at 17 factories, Alea.jl answers up to 11 factories (216 s) and runs out of memory at 12 factories and ProbLog answers up to 2 factories (3.9 s) and runs out of memory at 7 factories. tddlog leads on the weather factory, by days: it answers every size run, up to 1000 days (65 s), where Dice answers every size run, up to 1000 days (381 s), Alea.jl answers up to 9 days (57 s) and runs out of memory at 100 days and ProbLog answers up to 5 days (51 s) and runs out of memory at 6 days. In total time: against Dice, over the 44 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 1 024 s in all and Dice 3 269 s; over the 42 both answer, 420 s against 2 338 s; against Alea.jl's time without compilation, over the 33 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 88 s in all and Alea.jl 4 363 s; over the 27 both answer, 27 s against 763 s; against its process, over the 33 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 88 s in all and Alea.jl 4 679 s; over the 27 both answer, 27 s against 1 079 s; and against ProbLog, over the 18 instances that either answers, a run that does not answer counted at the 600 s limit, tddlog takes 60 s in all and ProbLog 4 892 s; over the 10 both answer, 0.3 s against 92 s. Answers that differ from the references: geni on geni_weather_n12 (zero), geni on geni_weather_n13 (zero), geni on geni_weather_n15 (zero), geni on geni_weather_n16 (zero) and geni on geni_weather_n17 (zero); tddlog's agree to 1.2e-13 relative.

findings.title: Further exact systems
paras: The survey of exact systems adds programs it runs on part of the suites, and each runs every program it can be given, compared with tddlog in the same run (a time under 0.2 s counted as 0.2 s). Per system: noDice answers 41 of 61; over the 55 given to both that either answers, noDice takes 10047 s and tddlog 89.6 s, both answering 41; Psi answers 13 of 57; over the 51 given to both that either answers, Psi takes 23411 s and tddlog 909 s, both answering 11; Pluck answers 3 of 4; over the 4 given to both that either answers, Pluck takes 616 s and tddlog 109 s, both answering 3, and Pluck is faster on 1; Storm sparse answers 145 of 252; over the 238 given to both that either answers, Storm sparse takes 60698 s and tddlog 1564 s, both answering 145, and Storm sparse is faster on 14; Storm exact answers 118 of 229; over the 215 given to both that either answers, Storm exact takes 61894 s and tddlog 913 s, both answering 118, and Storm exact is faster on 3; Storm dd answers 171 of 270; over the 254 given to both that either answers, Storm dd takes 59425 s and tddlog 1572 s, both answering 168; PRISM sparse answers 162 of 263; over the 246 given to both that either answers, PRISM sparse takes 62382 s and tddlog 2154 s, both answering 158, and PRISM sparse is faster on 8; PRISM hybrid answers 141 of 245; over the 228 given to both that either answers, PRISM hybrid takes 64305 s and tddlog 1823 s, both answering 137; Genfer answers 15 of 15; over the 15 given to both that either answers, Genfer takes 0.24 s and tddlog 123 s, and Genfer is faster on 8; SPPL answers 0 of 5; over the 5 given to both that either answers, SPPL takes 3000 s and tddlog 15.6 s, both answering 0; Geni answers 39 of 50; over the 44 given to both that either answers, Geni takes 4627 s and tddlog 1024 s, both answering 38. The tables of each suite give the instances.

findings.title: Answers
paras: tddlog's answers agree with the references everywhere, to 4e-10 relative against Alea.jl and exact references and to 5e-8 against ProbLog's eight printed digits. ProbLog's d-DNNF is wrong on one bit-blasted circuit (clickGraph at 14 bits, by 0.016), which Ganak's exact count confirms. Dice prints 0 for every answer on 8 bit-blasted circuits, and Alea.jl's discretization is defective in the far tails of a normal, which moves the gene expression program's answer at Figure 2's precision from 1/2 to 0.333 with 5 genes and 0.482 with 20, where the artifact's own runs give 0.4999995 at every number of genes.

suites.title: The Dice paper's programs
suites.about: The programs and Bayesian networks of the Dice paper (Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, OOPSLA 2020), a network as one Dice program per queried variable, and its loop programs scaled up. tddlog runs them translated to ProbLog, Alea.jl translated to Julia, Roulette translated to Racket. 300 s a run (600 s on the loop programs). noDice, Psi, Genfer, Storm and PRISM ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs or the ProbLog programs); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Storm and PRISM ran in a later run, on other machines, on the instances the release run did not give them, each beside tddlog: their times compare with that run's tddlog, not with the other columns, and the comparisons below use it.

suites.title: Alea.jl's and noDice's programs
suites.about: Cao et al.'s integer arithmetic programs (UAI 2023), Pluck's sequence models (PLDI 2025) and noDice's purely probabilistic programs (OOPSLA 2026). Alea.jl runs an Alea.jl program itself; tddlog and Dice run the Boolean circuit Alea.jl builds for it. The noDice programs are Dice programs, translated, and Roulette runs them translated to Racket. 600 s a run. noDice, Psi, Pluck, Storm and PRISM ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs or the ProbLog programs); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Storm and PRISM ran in a later run, on other machines, on the instances the release run did not give them, each beside tddlog: their times compare with that run's tddlog, not with the other columns, and the comparisons below use it.

suites.title: Bit-blasted programs
suites.about: The programs of the bit-blasting paper (Garg, Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, PLDI 2024) on ladders of precision. Alea.jl runs each program itself; tddlog runs the circuit Alea.jl builds for it. Dice's times on these circuits come from an earlier run, so they are in [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/benchmarks.md) and not here. 600 s a run. Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Storm and PRISM ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs or the ProbLog programs); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Storm and PRISM ran in a later run, on other machines, on the instances the release run did not give them, each beside tddlog: their times compare with that run's tddlog, not with the other columns, and the comparisons below use it. 29 more instances of the ladders no system ran: each system had failed on a smaller size.

suites.title: Roulette's programs
suites.about: The scaling programs of the Roulette paper (Moy et al., PLDI 2025) on ladders of size, and its nine Bayesian networks. Roulette runs the artifact's programs; tddlog, Dice and Alea.jl run programs of the same models. On caesar Roulette's time is that of its query with `#f`, which keeps the answer. 600 s a run. Storm and PRISM ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs or the ProbLog programs); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Storm and PRISM ran in a later run, on other machines, on the instances the release run did not give them, each beside tddlog: their times compare with that run's tddlog, not with the other columns, and the comparisons below use it.

suites.title: Geni's programs
suites.about: The programs of Geni's evaluation (Li and Zhang, ICFP 2025) that Dice runs: two grid networks and the weather factory, on ladders of size. ProbLog's d-DNNF and Roulette (on the Dice program translated to Racket) run beside the others here. 600 s a run. Geni, noDice, Psi, Storm and PRISM ran too, each on the programs it takes (its own paper's, the Dice programs or the ProbLog programs); a system's time is its process's, start-up included. Storm and PRISM ran in a later run, on other machines, on the instances the release run did not give them, each beside tddlog: their times compare with that run's tddlog, not with the other columns, and the comparisons below use it. Three more instances of the ladders no system ran: each system had failed on a smaller size.

setup: Three machines: a cloud machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, for the Alea.jl and noDice programs and the bit-blasted programs; a cloud machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, for the Dice paper's programs and Geni's programs and Roulette's programs; and a lab machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, for the earlier run of Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs. A run is one job that holds its machine alone. Programs run as independent jobs in lanes, each pinned to one logical CPU on its own physical core, with the machine's memory split between the lanes. In a lane all systems run on an instance back to back, in an order rotated by instance and repetition, so that the systems share the lanes alike.

The release run, all of its parts at one version of tddlog, each part with all of its systems in the same lanes: the arithmetic, sequence and noDice programs (60 lanes, 24 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); the networks, the Dice paper's programs and the loop programs (94 lanes, 15 GB a process, three repetitions, 300 s for the networks and the Dice paper's programs and 600 s for the loop programs, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); Roulette's programs (52 lanes, 28 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); the bit-blasted programs for tddlog and Alea.jl (45 lanes, 33 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19); and Geni's programs, with ProbLog's d-DNNF timed beside the others (49 lanes, 30 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 96 physical cores and 1488 GB of memory, 2026-10-19). Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs come from an earlier run (5 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, 2026-10-12) on the same circuits; neither those systems nor the circuits have changed since. Times compare within a run: on the bit-blasted programs the plots show tddlog and Alea.jl, and Dice's times are in the tables only. The plots of all programs put the runs together.

A program with a size runs from small to large, and a system that fails on one size (a timeout, out of memory, a crash) is not run on the larger sizes of that program; the tables mark those `skipped`, and they count as failures.
A time is the median of the repetitions, a failed repetition counted as longer than any time: of three repetitions, a system must answer in two.

For tddlog and Dice, the wall time of the process: parsing, compiling and answering every query. For Alea.jl, the time the program reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as the papers time it; the process's wall time, with Julia's start-up, loading Alea.jl and compiling its methods, is the dashed line in the plots and the "process" column in the tables. For Roulette, the time the artifact's own `time` reports for building and querying the program; the dashed line adds Racket's start-up and loading.

tddlog 0.1.0 (Rust 1.94.0, linked statically), one version for every part of the release run, which gave both its times and its answers, printed with 17 digits after the point. Dice 1.0 (the binary of the `sholtzen/dice` image), with an unlimited stack. Alea.jl at revision cf5e5b8 on Julia 1.11.9 with CUDD 3.0.0 and Distributions.jl 0.25.131, one thread. Roulette from its PLDI 2025 artifact (revision 54d6185 of its repository) on Racket 8.16, the paper's Racket being 8.13 ([docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md), section 11). ProbLog 2.3.0 with `-k ddnnf`, timed on Geni's programs, a clique-tree solver and dynamic programs over the models' states as references, and for the bit-blasted circuits that Alea.jl does not answer, exact weighted model counts by Ganak in rational arithmetic.

Geni (gennifer; Li and Zhang, ICFP 2025), noDice (Gürtler and Kaminski, OOPSLA 2026), Psi (Gehr et al., CAV 2016; revision ef8a9e5), Genfer (Zaiser, Murawski and Ong, NeurIPS 2023), SPPL 2.0.4 (Saad, Rinard and Mansinghka, PLDI 2021), Pluck (Bowers et al., PLDI 2025), Storm 1.14 (stormpy), one Sylvan thread (sparse, exact, dd) and PRISM 4.8.1 (sparse, hybrid). Their versions are those of [docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md).

CmdStan 2.32.2 (the paper's 2.28.2 does not build both of the artifact's array syntaxes), WebPPL 0.9.15 on node 18, and Psi at revision ef8a9e5, each on the artifact's own program of the model, in the earlier run, three seeds. AQUA and GuBPI were installed but not timed ([docs/baselines.md](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/docs/baselines.md), section 10): the artifact's AQUA inputs crash it or answer other quantities on all but four programs, and GuBPI's repository has programs for three of the models and prints bounds rather than an answer. Mathematica, with which the paper simplified Psi's integrals, is not available. Some of the artifact's sampler programs encode another model than the HyBit program: Stan's and WebPPL's weekend, and WebPPL's clinicalTrial2 and zeroone. The table marks them "another model" and gives, in a note, the answer of the model each encodes, worked out by hand; it is the value their estimates settle on.
